A_target.statement:
Let $f: \closedint a b \to \R$ be [[Definition:Continuous Real Function|continuous]] and $g: \closedint a b \to \R$ of [[Definition:Bounded Variation|bounded variation]].
Then the [[Definition:Riemann-Stieltjes Integral|Riemann-Stieltjes integral]] $\displaystyle \int_a^b f \rd g$ exists, and:
:$\displaystyle \int_a^b f \rd g = \bigintlimits {f g} a b - \int_a^b g \rd f$
whenever the right hand integral exists.

B_source.statement:
The [[Definition:Riemann Integral|Riemann integral]] is:
:$\displaystyle \int_a^b f \rd x = \lim_{\norm P \mathop \to 0} \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \map f {t_i} \paren {x_i - x_{i - 1} }$

substitutions.the subinterval length: the increment of the integrator across the subinterval
substitutions.the identity integrator: an arbitrary function of bounded variation

derived.existence of the limit of the sums: existence under bounded variation of the integrator

object_map.reformulation: Replace the length of each subinterval by the increment of a general integrator across it.

validity_conditions: Taking the integrator to be the identity makes each increment a subinterval length, recovering the Riemann integral exactly.
Bounded variation of the integrator bounds the total size of the increments, which is what replaces the automatic control of lengths and makes the sums converge.
Integrand and integrator must not share a discontinuity from the same side, or the sums depend on the tag placement and the integral fails to exist.
proof_plan:
Replace each length $x_i - x_{i - 1}$ by the increment $\map g {x_i} - \map g {x_{i - 1} }$:
:$\displaystyle \map S {P, f, g} = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \map f {t_i} \paren {\map g {x_i} - \map g {x_{i - 1} } }$

As $g$ has [[Definition:Bounded Variation|bounded variation]] $\map V g$:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \size {\map g {x_i} - \map g {x_{i - 1} } } \le \map V g$

$f$ is [[Definition:Uniformly Continuous Real Function|uniformly continuous]], so for two subdivisions of mesh $< \delta$:
:$\size {\map S {P, f, g} - \map S {Q, f, g} } \le 2 \epsilon \map V g$
Hence the sums are Cauchy and converge as the mesh tends to $0$.
Summation by parts on the sums gives the integration by parts formula.

With $\map g x = x$, the increments are the lengths, recovering the Riemann integral.
{{qed}}
